title: Memphis Dry Rub Ribs
seoTitle: Memphis Dry Rub Ribs | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Sticky bark, fall-off-bone ribs
description: Sticky bark, fall-off-bone ribs. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Memphis Dry Rub Ribs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Brown sugar, Paprika, Garlic powder, Onion powder as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Remove membrane
steps.instruction: Peel the silverskin off the bone side with a paper towel grip — it will not soften in smoke. Mix dry rub and coat both sides. Rest 30 minutes at room temp.

steps.title: Smoke 3-2-1 style
steps.instruction: Smoke at 250°F meat-side up for 3 hours. Spritz with apple juice if bark looks dry. Wrap in foil with a splash of juice for 2 hours. Unwrap, sauce if desired, finish 1 hour to set bark. Ribs bend without breaking when done.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes, slice between bones. Memphis dry rub ribs should have sticky bark and pull clean — not mush. Serve on trays; hold backup rack at 180°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Memphis Dry Rub Ribs onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Hold for late eaters
steps.instruction: Wrap cut ribs in foil on a sheet tray at 180°F up to 30 minutes. Spritz apple juice if edges look dry before the second tray goes out.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Memphis Dry Rub Ribs — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Memphis Dry Rub Ribs with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Memphis Dry Rub Ribs on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sticky bark, fall-off-bone ribs. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Memphis Dry Rub Ribs runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
